SO CF RU:18 - Heat Exchanger Int Fan

ru: SO CF RU:40 - Antenna
SO CF RU:64 - RUS, RRUS, AIR, mRRUS or Radio
SO CF I2A:33.d: There is an imbalance in signal strength between the receiver paths for one or more TRXs. Depending on which RX path has the lowest signal strength, one or more of the related faults are also raised. To avoid false alarms, the fault has a long filter time that depends on the traffic load. Therefore, the fault can occur several days after installation. Despite the long filter time, a single mobile might cause an alarm if the call is made when the traffic is low and the call continues for a long time in an area with poor coverage, for example, during nights and behind the antenna. When traffic increases, the alarm normally ceases. To correct this kind of alarm, the radio cell planning must be revised. This fault is also raised in cross-connection configurations if a cross-connected RUS/RRUS fails to forward RX signal to a dependent RUS/RRUS.
SO CF I2A:33.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. Note: Long filter time 0 do not use reset until all actions have been performed. Note: If other alarms are raised on the same RX path, this might also be the cause of the RX diversity alarm. If present, then correct such alarms first. • For RUG, follow the instructions in RBS 6000 DUG/RUG Troubleshooting Guidelines. • Use the raised RX I2A faults to identify which RXs, and thereby which RX path, are faulty. The RX path identifies the antenna connection to investigate. • If applicable, check that cables are connected to the correct antennas. The OMT Radio view shows how the IDB is defined regarding the connections. • Check that the correct RX Diversity mode is defined in the BSC (RX parameter RXD with possible values A, B, AB, and ABCD). See antenna setup in the OMT Radio view for help. • Check that all cross-connected RUSs/RRUSs are operational and can therefore supply RX signal to dependent RUSs/RRUSs. • If applicable, check that ALNA/TMAs are working correctly, for example, by monitoring the ALNA/TMA current power consumption with the OMT and comparing it with expected consumption. • Check all radio cables, connectors and other passive radio equipment, for example, with Antenna System VSWR tests. • Check the antennas/AIR.

SO CF I2A:47.d: For RUG-based configurations: Antenna hopping is not possible, either because of the configuration received from the BSC or site constraints. The BSS feature BTS Power Saving might raise this alarm when the traffic load is continuously low. The alarm has a filtering time of one week before the alarm is raised. To enable antenna hopping, at least one antenna system must include two enabled TXs, connected to separate antennas.
SO CF I2A:47.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check the BSC configuration of Antenna Hopping. • Read the IDB and use the Radio view in the OMT to check how the IDB is defined regarding the connections. • Undefine Antenna Hopping with the BSC if not feasible. Note: Manual definition of Antenna Hopping = On/Off in the IDB is overruled/redefined by the BSC configuration.

ru: SO CF RU:48 - GPS Receiver
SO CF RU:49 - GPS Receiver DXU Cable
SO CF I2A:48.d: For GPS receiver: • The defined GPS receiver has a hardware fault. If no backup synchronization source (PCM) is available, fault AO TF I1B:2 is raised. For GPS receiver DUG cable: • There is no communication between the DUG and the defined GPS receiver. If no backup synchronization source (PCM) is available, fault AO TF I1B:2 is raised.
SO CF I2A:48.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. For GPS receiver: • Remove the class 1 alarm, if present, by using PCM as backup synchronization source. This is done by defining the TF parameter SYNCSRC = DEFAULT in the BSC. • Check the GPS receiver and its receiver chain, that is, the antenna and cables. • Disconnect the power to the GPS receiver, for example, by disconnecting the connector in the OVP module. Wait a few minutes, then reconnect the power. For GPS receiver DUG cable: • Remove the class 1 alarm, if present, by using PCM as backup synchronization source. This is done by defining the TF parameter SYNCSRC = DEFAULT in the BSC. • Check the connection between the DUG and the GPS receiver. • Disconnect the power to the GPS receiver, for example, by disconnecting the connector in the OVP module. Wait a few minutes, then reconnect the power. • Check the power supply to the GPS receiver by checking the DC indicator in the OVP module. • Check the GPS receiver and its receiver chain, that is, the antenna and cables. • If no GPS receiver is required, then use Define GPS Parameters in the OMT to set GPS present = No in the IDB.

SO CF I2A:49.t: Battery Backup Time Shorter Than Expected
ru: SO CF RU:14 - Battery
SO CF I2A:49.d: An on demand or periodic battery test has indicated that the estimated remaining battery backup time is shorter than expected. The battery capacity may not be sufficient and the battery backup time is likely to be shorter than expected at the next AC power failure. The alarm is ceased when the following conditions exist: • The next battery test measures a battery backup time longer than the Minimum Backup Time defined in the IDB. Note: Repeated battery tests will cause battery discharge and aging of the batteries. The alarm is also ceased when the following conditions exist: • The Battery Installation Date battery test parameter is changed in the IDB after a battery replacement. • The Test Mode battery test parameter is set to DISABLED in the IDB. • The Shared Battery battery test parameter is changed in the IDB. • The Minimum State Of Health battery test parameter is changed in the IDB when the Shared Battery battery test parameter is set to TRUE and the Test Mode battery test parameter is set to CONFIGURED.
SO CF I2A:49.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Use the OMT to read the result of the latest battery test. • Verify that the battery test was properly performed and that the outcome was failed. • Check in the IDB that the battery test parameters are properly configured and that the Minimum Backup Time is correct. • If the battery is shared with any other RBS, verify that a battery test was performed at the same time on all RBS sharing the battery. • Check that no equipment other than this RBS (and possibly shared RBS) is connected to the battery. • Test the battery in accordance with the supplier specifications. • Check the condition of the battery and replace it if necessary.

SO CF I2A:50.d: The RBS is running on batteries. Unless external power is restored the RBS eventually turns itself off.

For SCUs, modify the defined Climate System or disconnect the SCU that mismatches. • Check that the node parameters defined for hub positions in the IDB correspond to the hub positions (valid and non-conflicting) used for the connected units. Otherwise, modify the IDB or connect the units to the hub positions defined in the IDB. • Check for faults in CPRI connectivity • Check the IDB for RE RI port connection. • Align the physical RE RI port connection, with the one specified above in the IDB. • If the actions above do not solve the problem. Change the CPRI cable. • In a ring topology configuration: Check the number of connected radio units and verify that it complies with the installed IDB. • Create a new IDB that applies to the RBS hardware and install it, using the OMT. • Reset the DUG.

SO CF I2A:57.d: This fault is raised if the difference in signal strength between two antennas in the same antenna system exceeds the limits defined by the Define RX Path Imbalance Parameters in the OMT. If the class 1 limit is exceeded, related fault AO TX I1B:35 is also raised and the TX disabled. The supervision of this fault is based on measurements over a long period; hence the fault does not cease as soon as the fault is corrected. The RX imbalance monitor must therefore be used to verify the correction of the fault.
SO CF I2A:57.a: Follow the instructions below: • For RUG, follow the instructions in RBS 6000 DUG/RUG Troubleshooting Guidelines. • For RUS, follow the instructions in RBS 6000 DUG/RUS Troubleshooting Guidelines. • Check the defined RX path invariance limits using the Define RX Path Imbalance Parameters function in the OMT for the faulty antenna system. • Check the TX cables/feeders, cable connections inside and outside the cabinet and antennas, for example, with Antenna System SWR tests. For information about how to perform an VSWR test, see document Verifying System Antennas or document Antenna System Tests for the relevant RBS. • When the fault is corrected, reset the RUG/RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio to cease the fault immediately. Note: If the fault is not resolved, it is reported again as soon as the minimum number of samples is collected.

SO CF I2A:59.t: Operating Temperature Too High, Main Load
ru: SO CF RU:31 - Environment
SO CF I2A:59.d: An alarm is raised when the main load is disconnected because the PDU temperature is too high. The likely cause is one of the following: • A fault in the climate system. • High ambient temperature. Power is disconnected from all equipment connected to outputs configured for main load.
SO CF I2A:59.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that all RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio circuit breakers on the PDU are switched on, and any fuses on the PDU are intact. • Check for other temperature-related alarms from this RBS. • Check if the problem is caused by high ambient temperature. • Resolve any external RBS temperature problems. • Check if the problem is caused by a fault in the RBS climate system. • Resolve any RBS climate system problems. • Restart the PDU. • Replace the PDU. • If the alarm soon reappears, the PDU is probably not faulty, and the problem is probably a general climate system problem.

SO CF I2A:60.t: Operating Temperature Too High, Battery Disconnected
ru: SO CF RU:31 - Environment
SO CF I2A:60.d: An alarm is raised when the battery is disconnected because the BFU temperature is too high or a risk for thermal runaway is detected. The battery is reconnected when the BFU temperature falls; or reconnected after 24 hours if it’s caused by detection of a thermal runaway risk. The likely cause is one of the following: • A fault in the climate system. • High ambient temperature. • A BFU fault. • A risk for thermal runaway detected. The battery backup system is disconnected, and the RBS is unable to function in the event of an AC power failure. The alarm should be re-raised after system restart during a period of 24 hours if it was raised by detection of thermal runaway risk.
SO CF I2A:60.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check if the problem is caused by detection of thermal runaway risk. • Check if the problem is caused by high ambient temperature. • Resolve any external RBS temperature problems. • Check if other units in the same cabinet have raised temperature-related alarms, which can indicate high ambient temperature or a fault in the climate system of the cabinet containing the BFU. • Check if the problem is caused by a fault in the RBS climate system. • Resolve any RBS climate system problems. • Restart the BFU. • Replace the BFU. • If the alarm soon reappears, the BFU is probably not faulty, and the problem is probably a general climate system problem.

SO CF I2A:61.t: Operating Temperature Too High, Capacity Reduced
ru: SO CF RU:31 - Environment
SO CF I2A:61.d: The likely cause of the alarm is one of the following: An alarm is raised when the PSU operating temperature is too high and PSU performance deteriorates. • High temperatures can cause reduced PSU output power. • PDU operating temperature is too high. • E-fuse on PDU / ECM operating temperature is too high.
SO CF I2A:61.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check for other temperature-related alarms from this RBS. • Check if the problem is caused by high ambient temperature. • Resolve any external RBS temperature problems. • Check if the problem is caused by a fault in the RBS climate system. • Resolve any RBS climate system problems. • Restart the PSU. • Replace the ECM. • Replace the PSU. • If the alarm soon reappears, the PSU is probably not faulty, and the problem is probably a general climate system problem.

SO CF I2A:62.t: Operating Temperature Too Low, Capacity Reduced
ru: SO CF RU:31 - Environment
SO CF I2A:62.d: An alarm is raised when the PSU operating temperature is too low, causing reduced PSU performance. Low temperatures can cause PSU output power to fall below the minimum level required to power the RBS.
SO CF I2A:62.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check for other temperature-related alarms from this RBS. • Check if the problem is caused by low ambient temperature. • Resolve any external RBS temperature problems. • Check if the problem is caused by a fault in the RBS climate system. • Resolve any RBS climate system problems. • Restart the PSU. • Replace the PSU. • If the alarm soon reappears, the PSU is probably not faulty, and the problem is probably a general climate system problem.

SO CF I2A:63.t: Operating Temperature Too High, No Service
ru: SO CF RU:31 - Environment
SO CF I2A:63.d: An alarm is raised when the PSU or SU (Power Supply) operating temperature is too high (near the destructive range), causing it to stop supplying power to the RBS. Power to the RBS is reduced and there is a risk of the RBS ceasing to function.
SO CF I2A:63.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check for other temperature-related alarms from this RBS. • Check if the problem is caused by high ambient temperature. • Resolve any external RBS temperature problems. • Check if the problem is caused by a fault in the RBS climate system. • Resolve any RBS climate system problems. • Restart the PSU. • Replace the PSU. • Check if the fault is caused by SU. • Replace the faulty SU. • If the alarm soon reappears, the PSU or SU is probably not faulty, and the problem is probably a general climate system problem.

SO CF I2A:64.t: Operating Temperature Too Low, Communication Lost
ru: SO CF RU:31 - Environment
SO CF I2A:64.d: An alarm is raised before the PSU operating temperature is too low, causing the loss of DU communication. This can reduce both the performance of RBS power system control functions and the power to the RBS.
SO CF I2A:64.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check for other temperature-related alarms from this RBS. • Check if the problem is caused by low ambient temperature. • Resolve any RBS external temperature problems. • Check if the problem is caused by a fault in the RBS climate system. • Resolve any RBS climate system problems. • Restart the PSU. • Replace the PSU. • If the alarm soon reappears, the PSU is probably not faulty, and the problem is probably a general climate system problem.

SO CF I2A:65.t: Battery Voltage Too Low, Main Load Disconnected
SO CF I2A:65.d: An alarm is raised when the main load is disconnected because of low battery voltage. This is normal when the RBS runs for too long on battery backup after an AC power failure. All equipment connected to outputs configured for main load is disconnected.
SO CF I2A:65.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that AC power is available or wait until it is. • Check that sufficient battery capacity is available or install more if necessary. • Check that the correct voltage is set for IDB parameter MainLoadUndervoltageDisconnect. • Check that the battery is connected correctly. • Check the battery cables and replace any faulty cables. • Restart the BFU. • Replace the BFU. • Check the condition of the battery and replace it if necessary.

SO CF I2A:66.t: Battery Voltage Too Low, Prio Load Disconnected
SO CF I2A:66.d: An alarm is raised when the battery is disconnected because of low battery voltage. This is normal when the RBS runs for too long on battery backup after an AC power failure. All power distribution ceases.
SO CF I2A:66.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that AC power is available. • Check that sufficient battery capacity is available or install more if necessary. • Check that the correct voltage is set for IDB parameter PriorityLoadUndervoltageDisconnect. • Check that the battery is connected correctly. • Check the battery cables and replace any faulty cables. • Restart the BFU. • Replace the BFU. • Check the condition of the battery and replace it if necessary.

ru: SO CF RU:31 - Environment
SO CF I2A:67.d: An alarm is raised when the system voltage falls below a set level.
SO CF I2A:67.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. AC/DC rectification or DC/DC conversion power system: • Check that alarm levels are set correctly. • Check the incoming power. • Check that enough PSUs are installed and, install more if necessary. • Replace any faulty PSUs. -48 V DC direct power system: • Check that alarm levels are set correctly. • Check the incoming power.

ru: SO CF RU:31 - Environment
SO CF I2A:68.d: An alarm is raised when the system voltage rises above a set limit. If the system voltage continues to rise, services can fail and RBS equipment can be damaged. When the alarm raise criteria is fulfilled, control system should order disconnect of battery in charging direction and set the charging voltage to a “Fail Safe Charging Voltage” (52V). When the alarm is ceased, control system should connect the battery using soft start. AC/DC rectification or DC/DC conversion power system: • A PSU supplies excessive voltage. -48 V DC direct power system: • Voltage of incoming power is too high.
SO CF I2A:68.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. AC/DC rectification or DC/DC conversion power system: • Check that the system voltage is correct by measuring it through the PDU port. • Replace the PDU if the system voltage is correct and the alarm is still raised. • Replace any faulty PSU. -48 V DC direct power system: • Check the incoming power. • Check that the system voltage is correct by measuring it through the PDU port. • Replace the PDU if the system voltage is correct and the alarm is still raised.

SO CF I2A:69.d: The ability to keep a consistent product data view is lost and there is a mismatch between configured data and unit-provided data. This alarm is raised if the configuration data does not match the cabinet product data, stored internally in the RBS (in the SCU/SUP). The alarm is raised if the SCU is moved from another RBS to this RBS, because the product data, stored in the SCU/SUP, does not match the original data stored in the DU. Correct cabinet product data (PID) is not available for this RBS. There is a risk that the RBS is not working correctly.
SO CF I2A:69.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Add the values stated on the cabinet enclosure label to the IDB description.

ru: SO CF RU:14 - Battery
SO CF I2A:70.d: An alarm is raised if the battery voltage indicates that an expected battery is not present. The likely cause is one of the following: • A disconnected or faulty cable between the battery and the BFU. • A faulty battery. The battery backup system is disconnected, and the RBS is unable to function in the event of an AC power failure.
SO CF I2A:70.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that the battery is present. • Check that the battery is connected correctly. • Check the battery cables and replace any faulty cables. • Restart the BFU. • Replace any faulty BFU. • Check the condition of the battery and replace it if necessary.

SO CF I2A:71.d: An alarm is raised if the voltage is too low during intermittent charging. The battery voltage reached the set limit while the battery was disconnected during intermittent charging. Battery capacity is lower than expected. The backup time at the next AC power failure is likely to be shorter than expected.
SO CF I2A:71.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that the voltage for intermittent charging, IDB parameter IntermittentChargeConnectVoltage, is set correctly. • Check the battery condition, for example, by performing an on-demand battery test. • Check the condition of the battery and replace it if necessary.

SO CF I2A:72.d: The DUG is unable to download software to one or more RUSs/RRUSs/AIRs/mRRUSs/Radios marked as expected in the IDB.
SO CF I2A:72.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Perform an unconditional software download to RBS from the BSC or use the OMT to load new software on the flash card.

SO CF I2A:73.t: Degraded or Lost Communication to Radio Unit
SO CF I2A:73.d: The DUG, or a RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio in a cascade chain, has no contact or degraded communication with one or more RUSs/RRUSs/AIRs/mRRUSs/Radios marked as expected in the IDB.
SO CF I2A:73.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • For RUS, follow the instructions in RBS 6000 DUG/RUS Troubleshooting Guidelines. • Check that all RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio circuit breakers on the PDU are switched on and that all fuses on the PDU are intact. • Check that all RUSs/RRUSs/AIRs/mRRUSs/Radios are powered-on. • Check that all defined RUSs/RRUSs/AIRs/m RRUSs/Radios in the IDB correspond to the RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio in the RBS. Otherwise modify the IDB. • Check that the radio interface cables from the DUG to and between all RUSs/RRUSs/AIRs/mRRUSs/Radio are correctly connected and in good condition. • If fault occurs on an AIR where both radio units are configured for mixed mode between GSM and another Radio Access Network (RAN), check that the other network is capable of running mixed mode on both radio units. • Reset the RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio not communicating correctly. • Reset the DUG. • Use the OMT function Check IDB to identify hardware/IDB inconsistence. • Replace the radio interface cable between the DUG and the RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio, or between RUSs/RRUSs/AIRs/mRRUSs/Radio in the cascade chain. • Replace the SFP on the units that are not communicating correctly. • Replace the RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio that is not communicating correctly. • Replace the DUG.

SO CF I2A:74.d: The DUG in IDL2 TG-Cluster, has no communication over one or more ports defined for IDL2 communication in the IDB.
SO CF I2A:74.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that all DUs in IDL2 TG-Cluster are powered-on. • Check that cabling is connecting defined RI ports for TG-cluster according to IDB. Otherwise modify the IDB or reconnect cable according to the defined RI Ports. • Check that all the DU to DU CPRI cables from the DU to another are correctly connected and in good condition. • Use the OMT function Check IDB to identify hardware/IDB inconsistence. • Reset the slave DU not communicating correctly. • Reset the master DU. • Replace the DU to DU CPRI cable between the DUs in IDL2 TG-Cluster. • Replace the SFP on the units that are not communicating correctly. • Replace the Slave DU that is not communicating correctly. • Replace the master DU.

SO CF I2A:75.t: SW Version Mismatch in CPRI based TG-Cluster
SO CF I2A:75.d: In an IDL2 TG cluster, different versions of the software are used in the Master DU and Slave DU.
SO CF I2A:75.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Replace the software, ensuring that the software version used is the same on both the Master and the Slave nodes.

SO CF I2A:76.t: Node Group Sync Communication over IDL2 Lost
SO CF I2A:76.d: The fault is raised by the Slave DUG when the Slave DUG loses NGS communication over IDL2 with the Master DUG in a Node Group.
SO CF I2A:76.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • If raised together with SO CF I2A:74/DU to DU Communication Lost • • See action for SO CF I2A:74. • Check that all DUs in the Node Group are powered-on. • Check that cabling is connecting defined RI ports for TG-cluster according to IDB. Otherwise modify the IDB or reconnect cable according to the defined RI Ports. • Check that all the DU to DU CPRI cables from the DU to another are correctly connected and in good condition. • Use the OMT function Check IDB to identify hardware/IDB inconsistence. • Reset the slave DU not communicating correctly. • Reset the master DU. • Replace the DU to DU CPRI cable between the DUs in the Node Group. • Replace the SFP on the units that are not communicating correctly. • Replace the Slave DU that is not communicating correctly. • Replace the master DU.

ru: SO CF RU:67 - SU
SO CF I2A:77.d: An alarm is raised if there is a disconnection between the unit and some of superior units (not all superior units).
SO CF I2A:77.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Find the disconnected unit. • Check that the unit is correctly connected to the superior units. • Replace or reconnect the cable between the unit and the superior units. • Replace or reconnect the unit.

SO CF I2A:79.d: There is a configuration fault of CPRI System.
SO CF I2A:79.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that the defined DUs correspond to the DUs in the RBS and are connected to the right RI port according to the IDB. Otherwise modify the IDB. • Check that the TRX to MCTR relationship in the IDB is correctly set up. • Reset the DUG. • Replace the DUG.

SO CF I2A:80.t: Antenna System DC Power Supply Overloaded
ru: SO CF RU:40 - Antenna
SO CF I2A:80.d: The DC power supply of the antenna system is overloaded. This can be caused by a hardware failure or a short circuit. Most likely: jumper, feeder or TMA. Less likely: RUS output or other RBS internal RF cables connecting to jumper. If the RUS/RRUS/AIR/Radio output is overloaded, the RUS/RRUS/AIR/Radio automatically protects itself by switching the DC output power off.
SO CF I2A:80.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Inspect all feeder cables, radio cables, connectors and other passive radio equipment. • Inspect the antennas/AIR. • Check that ALNA/TMAs are working correctly, for example, by monitoring the ALNA/TMA current power consumption with the OMT and comparing it with expected consumption. • Inspect the TX cables/feeders, cable connections inside and outside the cabinet and antennas/AIR, for example, with Antenna System SWR tests or DC resistance measurements. For information about how to perform an SWR test see documents Verifying System Antennas or Antenna System Tests in the CPI for the relevant RBS. • Confirm with the OMT that the IDB is correct regarding installed antenna system. If not, then modify and install a new IDB. • Check that cables are connected to the correct antennas. The OMT Radio view shows how the IDB is defined regarding the connections. • Reset RUS/RRUS/AIR/Radio • Use the OMT function Check IDB to identify hardware/IDB inconsistencies. • Replace the RUS/RRUS/AIR/Radio.

SO CF I2A:81.d: The DUG has no contact with the primary DU.
SO CF I2A:81.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that the defined primary DU corresponds to the DU in the RBS. Otherwise modify the IDB. • Check that the EC bus between the DUG and the primary DU is correctly connected and in good condition. • Reset the DUG. • Reset the primary DU.

ru: SO CF RU:64 - RUS, RRUS, AIR, mRRUS or Radio
SO TRXC RU:25 - RUS, RRUS, AIR, mRRUS or Radio
SO CF I2A:82.d: A Radio Unit is not compatible with GSM. This can for example be caused by connecting to a RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio with a non-GSM compatible frequency band, or connecting to a Radio Unit for another radio access standard.
SO CF I2A:82.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Use the OMT function Check IDB to identify hardware/IDB inconsistencies. • Replace the Radio Unit with a GSM compatible RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio.

SO CF I2A:83.d: The DUG cannot connect to one or more RUSs/RRUSs/AIRs/mRRUSs/Radios configured for mixed mode between GSM and another Radio Access Network (RAN). Even though the RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio is visible for the DUG, it is not possible to establish a connection on the application layer.
SO CF I2A:83.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that all RUSs/RRUSs/AIRs/mRRUSs/Radios are available for GSM. If the other RAN has a RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio reserved for single access, force that RAN to release the RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio. • Reset the RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio not communicating correctly with the DUG. • Reset the DUG. • Use the OMT function Check IDB to identify hardware/IDB inconsistencies. • Replace the radio interface cable between the DUG and the RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio. • Replace the RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio not communicating correctly with the DUG. • Replace the DUG.

SO CF I2A:84.d: An unauthorized access (hunt) using incoming OSE signals has been performed by an external process.
SO CF I2A:84.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • If the fault is not ceased after 1 hour, search for unauthorized equipment connected to the CPRI cable on the site. • Disconnect the unauthorized equipment. The fault cease after 1 hour.

SO CF I2A:85.d: The IDB does not match the RBS hardware. The RBS is configured for a single TX RUS but a dual TX RUS is connected. This is a warning that only half of the available TX functionality is being used in relation to the capacity of the connected RUS.
SO CF I2A:85.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Use the OMT function Check IDB to identify hardware/IDB inconsistencies. • Check that the correct RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Rad io hardware is installed. • Check that each RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio is connected to the correct RI port on the DUG. • If the full TX RUS capacity is to be used: Create a new IDB that uses the full capacity of the new RUS, use the OMT to install the new IDB, and reset the DUG.

ru: SO CF RU:14 - Battery
SO CF I2A:86.d: An on demand or periodic battery test has indicated that the battery capacity is lower than expected. The estimated battery state of health is less than expected and the battery backup time is likely to be shorter than expected at the next AC power failure. The alarm is ceased when the following conditions exist: • Next battery test measures a battery state of health greater than the Minimum State Of Health defined in the IDB. Note: Repeated battery tests will cause battery discharge and aging of the batteries. The alarm is also ceased when the following conditions exist: • The Battery Installation Date battery test parameter is changed in the IDB after a battery replacement. • The Test Mode battery test parameter is set to DISABLED in the IDB. • The Shared Battery battery test parameter is changed in the IDB. • The Minimum State Of Health battery test parameter is changed in the IDB when the Shared Battery battery test parameter is set to TRUE and the Test Mode battery test parameter is set to CONFIGURED.
SO CF I2A:86.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Use the OMT to read the result of the latest battery test. • Verify that the battery test was properly performed and that the outcome was failed. • Check in the IDB that the battery test parameters are properly configured, the Minimum State of Health is correct and the Shared Battery is set to FALSE. • Check that no other RBS or other equipment than this RBS is connected to the battery. • Test the battery in accordance with the supplier specifications. • Check the condition of the battery and replace it if necessary.

ru: SO CF RU:64 - RUS, RRUS, AIR, mRRUS or Radio
SO CF I2A:87.d: There are internal hardware faults in one or more RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio, the RUS power supply or in some device, that is, a feeder or TMA consuming too much power. The severities of the faults are indicated by the related faults.
SO CF I2A:87.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Follow the instructions in the related faults. • Check the feeder cables, especially that they are connected to the correct ports on the ALNA/TMA. • Check that ALNA/TMAs are working correctly, for example, by monitoring the ALNA/TMA current power consumption with the OMT and comparing it with expected consumption. • Switch off the power to the pinpointed RUSs/RRUSs/AIRs/mRRUSs/Radio. Wait at least 10 seconds and switch on the power. • Replace the RUSs/RRUSs/AIRs/mRRUSs/Radio. Note: It can take up to ten minutes for the alarm to cease.

SO CF I2A:88.d: The BTS has calculated the length of CPRI cables for the active path or for the redundant path that will be used if the normal active path cannot be used. The calculated delay over CPRI cables towards an RE has resulted in too long delay time, corresponding to a cable length exceeding 40 km. The length of the path exceeds the supported maximum length of the cables. This means that there is a risk that the active path cannot be used or that there is a risk that the redundant path cannot be used if the normal active path is broken.
SO CF I2A:88.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Ensure that the CPRI cable length is shorter than 40 km.

ru: SO CF RU:0 - DXU, DUG 10, DUG 20, MU or IXU
SO CF I2A:89.d: There is an internal fault in one or more TRXs/RXs/TXs. The traffic on one or more extension TRXs is not started.
SO CF I2A:89.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Follow the instructions in the related faults. • Reset the DUG. • Replace the DUG.

SO CF I2A:90.d: The ring redundancy in a ring topology CPRI chain has been lost. Traffic capacity is maintained but traffic capacity will be lost if another communication break occurs.
SO CF I2A:90.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that all RUS/RRUS/Radio circuit breakers on the PDU are switched on and that all fuses on the PDU are intact. • Check that all RUSs/RRUSs/Radios are powered-on. • Check that all defined RUSs/RRUSs/Radios in the IDB correspond to the RUS/RRUS/Radio in the RBS. Otherwise modify the IDB. • Check that the radio interface cables from the DUG to and between all RUSs/RRUSs/Radios are correctly connected and in good condition. • Reset the RUS/RRUS/Radio that is not communicating correctly. • Replace the radio interface cable between the DUG and the RUS/RRUS/Radio, or between RUSs/RRUSs/Radio in the cascade chain. • Replace the SFP on the units that are not communicating correctly. • Replace the RUS/RRUS/Radio that is not communicating correctly.

ru: SO CF RU:63 - SCU or SUP
SO CF I2A:91.d: SCU Power connector is faulty / missing. The cooling capability of RBS is reduced
SO CF I2A:91.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check the failing power contact • Check the PDU switch that powers the SCU • If applicable, connect the missing power contact to the SCU or enable the fuse that powers the SCU. • Reset the SCU. • Replace the SCU.

SO CF I2A:92.d: The DUG has no contact with the secondary node.
SO CF I2A:92.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that the number of external nodes in the IDB is consistent with the number of secondary nodes installed in the RBS. • Check that the other nodes in the RBS are configured as secondary nodes. • Check that the hub position of the external node’s child EcPort in this node has the same value as the hub position of the PlugInUnit́s child EcPort in the corresponding secondary node/nodes. • In primary node, perform the following steps below only if any additional HW unit reports that it is disconnected from the EC bus. • Check that the primary node is properly connected to the EC bus hub/SHU. • Replace the cable that connects the primary node to the EC bus. • Restart the primary node. • Check that the secondary node is properly connected to the EC bus hub/SHU. • Replace the cable that connects the secondary node to the EC bus. • Restart the secondary node. • Restart the primary node. • Replace the secondary node. • Replace the primary node. • Replace the EC bus hub/SHU.

SO CF I2A:93.d: A configuration fault has been detected for one or more external alarm ports on an RRUS. The fault indicates the inconsistent configuration of alarm activation criteria for one or more alarm ports used by more than one RBS node. The external alarm port cannot be used to indicate alarms until the fault is corrected.
SO CF I2A:93.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • After coordination with the other RBSs using the port, reconfigure affected External Alarm port/ports

ru: SO CF RU:40 - Antenna
SO CF RU:64 - RUS, RRUS, AIR, mRRUS or Radio
SO CF I2A:94.d: Malfunction detected in antenna system or AIR/mRRUS.
SO CF I2A:94.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. If mRRUS with Internal Antenna or AIR: • Check that the defined parameters in the IDB regarding External Antenna and Feeder Supervision are correct. • Reset the AIR/mRRUS. • Replace the AIR/mRRUS If mRRUS with External Antenna: • Check that the defined parameters in the IDB are correct. • Check the feeder cables and RF cable connections at the radio unit and at the antenna. • Reset the mRRUS.

SO CF I2A:95.d: The DX CPU utilization has been high, that is, greater than 90 %, for 60 seconds. During Function Change it is normal to get high CPU utilization during loading of SW to Radio Units.

ru: SO CF RU:31 - Environment
SO CF I2A:96.d: This fault bit will be raised when the fan speed has been running over the threshold value 90% for the defined supervision time period. The supervision time period is settable in OMT to the predefined values: 6 h, 12 h or 24 h. If the operator has not chosen any of the predefined values the supervision period is by default set to 12 h. The “Fan Speed Continuously High” supervision functionality may be turned off by setting the supervision period to 0 (ZERO) h.
SO CF I2A:96.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. Check if the following alarms are present, and resolve them if they are: AlarmMO No ConnectionFanGroup/FieldReplaceableUnit Fan FailiureFanGroup Fan PowerCabinet Clogged Air FilterCabinet If the alarm remains, examine the site conditions: • Check that the site has been built correctly, in line with the installation guidelines. • Check that there is enough cooling capacity in the area, for example an appropriate number of AC units. • Check that all airflow paths are free, and that there is sufficient free space at air inlets and outlets. • Check that the ambient and supply air temperatures for the RBS are within the calculated normal range. • If unexpected temperature or flaws are found, it implies that the site is unsuitable for the equipment. Contact site personnel for appropriate actions, then check if the alarm has ceased. • If the alarm remains, and the unit is mounted in a cabinet, check the climate system on the site for failures and correct them: • Check that the climate equipment is properly installed and operational. • Check that fans, coolers, and heaters run as expected with regards to temperature conditions. • Check that no dummy units are missing or incorrectly installed. • For outdoor cabinets, check that equipment such as thermosiphon systems and heat exchangers are working properly and have free and clean air paths. • If the alarm remains, consult the next level of maintenance support.

ru: SO CF RU:67 - SU
SO CF I2A:97.d: This alarm is raised when electric current becomes too high on one of the output ports on an SU (Power Supply).
SO CF I2A:97.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Find the faulty SU. • Replace the SU.

SO CF EC1:2.d: The DUG is in full maintenance mode and cannot be controlled by the BSC.
SO CF EC1:2.a: The DUG can be brought into no maintenance mode by pressing the Maintenance button on the DUG or using the function Change Local/Remote State in Local OMT, Remote OMT, or Remote OMT over IP.

SO CF EC1:4.d: The DUG is in full maintenance mode and cannot be controlled by the BSC.
SO CF EC1:4.a: The DUG can be brought into no maintenance mode by pressing the Maintenance button on the DUG or using the function Change Local/Remote State in Local OMT, Remote OMT, or Remote OMT over IP.

SO CF EC1:5.t: L/R TI (Local to Remote While Link Lost)
SO CF EC1:5.d: The DUG went into no maintenance mode while the CF link was down. Note: For information only.

SO TRXC I1A:24.d: The temperature of the RUG/RUS/RRUS/AIR/m RRUS/Radio is in the non-destruction range. The fault ceases when the temperature is back within the exceptional-operation range. In the non-destruction range the RUS/RRUS/AIR/ mRRUS/Radio takes autonomous actions to protect itself from being damaged. No function is guaranteed. When the fault ceases the system restarts the RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio to ensure functionality. In the exceptional operation range the RUS/RRUS/AI R/mRRUS/Radio has full functionality and degraded performance. The likely causes of this fault are as follows: • If the fault is issued together with a fan fault, then the most likely cause of the fault is a faulty fan unit. • If the alarm is raised on only one RUG/RUS/RRUS /AIR/mRRUS/Radio, then it is likely that the unit has developed a fault, in which case it is likely that another fault also has been issued for that unit. • If several radio units from different subracks have issued the fault, then the most likely cause is a fault at the site, in the RBS air-conditioning or in the cooling system.
SO TRXC I1A:24.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • For RUS, follow the instructions in RBS 6000 DUG/RUS Troubleshooting Guidelines. • If applicable, make sure dummy plates and air guides are correctly installed in the RBS. • Inspect the site cooling and heating systems to ensure that they are functioning correctly. • Inspect the RBS/RRU to ensure that there are no leaks and that nothing is obstructing the airflow in or around the unit issuing the alarm. Before inspecting an RRUS/Radio, remove the front cover. • Test the climate system. • Reset the RUG/RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio. • Use the OMT function Check IDB to identify hardware/IDB inconsistencies • Replace the RUG/RUS/RRUS/AIR/mRRUS/Radio. Note: It may take up to ten minutes before the alarm is ceased.

AO TF I1A:0.d: An alarm is raised if the OVCXO temperature falls below the operational temperature. The oscillator frequency depends on temperature. Too low an OVCXO temperature causes timing function disturbances.
AO TF I1A:0.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check for other temperature-related alarms from this RBS. • Check if the problem is caused by low ambient temperature. • Resolve any RBS external temperature problems. • Check if the problem is caused by a fault in the RBS climate system. • Resolve any RBS climate system problems. • Replace any faulty RBS external equipment.

AO TF I2A:0.d: Frame synchronization cannot be maintained for the RBS. If no related faults are present, the frame synchronization will probably recover after a few hours.
AO TF I2A:0.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. If GPS reference: • Block/deblock the TF. • Check that the GPS antenna is positioned so that it can receive signals from a sufficient number of satellites all the time. • Check the connection between the DUG and the GPS receiver. • Check the GPS receiver and its receiver chain, that is, antenna, cables, and so on. If NGS reference: • Block/deblock the TF. • Check that incoming synchronization to the Synchronization Provider is without faults. If the Synchronization Provider has lost its RNT (Radio Network Time) sync source, the time accuracy for a synchronized radio network cannot be guaranteed. Check the DUW/DUL/DUS documentation for further analysis. • Check that cabling is connecting defined RI ports for NGS according to IDB. Otherwise modify the IDB or reconnect cable according to the defined RI Ports. • If RNT synch source was permanently removed from Synchronization Provider, perform a power off/power on of the DUG.

AO TF EC1:0.d: There are several options: If TF mode is set to slave (TG parameter TFMODE = SA in the BSC) and ESB is used: • The RBS has tried to synchronize with the External Synchronization Bus (ESB) reference, used as TG synchronization source, for 5 minutes but failed. • TF has been in holdover mode because of failing ESB reference and the ESB did not recover before the holdover timeout. • The alarm is sometimes raised and almost immediately ceased if the master TG is reset. If TF mode is set to Slave (TG parameter TFMODE = SA in the BSC) and IDL2 is used: • The RBS has tried to synchronize with the IDL2 reference, used as TG synchronization source, for 5 minutes but failed. • TF has been in holdover mode because of failing IDL2 reference and the IDL2 did not recover before the holdover timeout. • The alarm is sometimes raised and almost immediately ceased if the master TG is reset. Note: The holdover period can be extended from 2 minutes up to 24 hours if TF holdover mode is set to Intercell in the IDB. This requires that no TRXs in the RBS are included in a cell together with TRXs from a different RBS. If TF mode is set to standalone or master (TG parameter TFMODE = SA or MA in the BSC) and NGS is used: • The RBS has tried to synchronize with the external reference (NGS, GPS or PCM) for 5 minutes but failed. • TF has been in holdover mode because of failing reference (NGS, GPS or PCM) and it did not recover before the holdover timeout. If TF mode is set to standalone or master (TG parameter TFMODE = SA or MA in the BSC) and GPS is used: • The RBS has tried to synchronize with the GPS reference for 5 minutes but failed and no PCM is defined as backup synchronization source. • TF has been in holdover mode because of failing GPS reference and the GPS reference did not recover before the holdover timeout.
AO TF EC1:0.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. If ESB reference: • Check that synchronization of the master TG is without faults. • Check that the master TG has TF mode = master defined (TG parameter TFMODE = M in the BSC). • Check the hardware of the master TF source, (DXU if RBS 2000, DUG if RBS6000). • Check that the ESB cables between the master TG and slave TG are correctly connected and undamaged. If the cable is damaged, then replace it. • Check that termination plugs are mounted on all unconnected ESB connectors. If IDL2 reference: • If raised together with SO CF I2A:75/SW Version Mismatch in CPRI based TG-Cluster • • See action for SO CF I2A:75 • If raised together with SO CF I2A:74/DU to DU Communication Lost • • See action for SO CF I2A:74. • Check that synchronization of the master TG is without faults. • Check that the master TG has TF mode = master defined (TG parameter TFMODE = MA in the BSC). • Check the hardware of the master TF source (DUG). • Check that the IDL2 cables between the master TG and slave TG are correctly connected and undamaged. If the cable is damaged, then replace it. If NGS reference: • If raised together with AO TF EC2:50/ Node Group Synch Source Lost • • See action for AO TF EC2:50 • Check that incoming synchronization of the SP (Synchronization Provider) is without faults. Check the DUW/DUL/DUS documentation for further analysis. • Check that cabling is connecting defined RI ports for NGS according to IDB. Otherwise modify the IDB or reconnect cable according to the defined RI Ports. If GPS reference: • Use PCM as backup synchronization source. This is done by defining the TF parameter SYNCSRC = DEFAULT in the BSC. • Check the GPS antenna. • Check the connection between the GPS receiver and the GPS antenna. • Check that the GPS antenna is placed so that it can receive signals from a sufficient number of satellites all the time. If it is not, move the GPS antenna.

AO TF EC1:1.d: The synchronization reference from the PCM network is faulty (for example, too much jitter/wander) or missing. More information can be found in Transmission System Supervision in the CPI for the relevant RBS. The alarm is raised if the following applies: • TF has been trying to synchronize with the PCM reference for more than 5 minutes after initial startup. • TF has detected that the PCM reference has drifted more than 80 ppb during the last 48h. • If a second PCM reference is not available and the TF did not recover before the holdover period expired (that is, the AO TF EC2:1 alarm was active for too long.) • The holdover period depends on how long it takes for the variance of the TF estimated frequency to exceed a variance limit for a class 1 alarm. The limit is set to ensure that the frequency at the antenna does not exceed the 50 ppb accuracy limit. • Explanation:When the reference quality of the PCM is outside specification of G.823 and G.824, the BTS goes into holdover and the TF starts to estimate its own frequency quality. The trigger to go into holdover and start the estimation is when short-term wander on the PCM reference is more than 6 ppm for 25 seconds. The estimation process, using a Kalman filter, causes the variance of the estimated frequency to increase with time. • The alarm is raised after about 24 h when the temperature varies within +-10°C if the following conditions are fulfilled: • RBS with DUG or DXU excluding DXU-01, DXU-03, DXU-11 • More than 72 hours of operation locked to PCM, with temperature supervision. • PCM reference traceable to G.812 Type II/Stratum 2 • The alarm is raised after about 60 minutes if the above conditions are not fulfilled. Note: Only when TF mode is master or stand-alone.
AO TF EC1:1.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • For RUG, follow the instructions in RBS 6000 DUG-RUG Troubleshooting Guidelines. • For RUS, follow the instructions in RBS 6000 DUG-RUS Troubleshooting Guidelines. • Check the PCM quality with the BSC printout command DTQUP: DIP. • Check that the transmission parameters are correctly set in the IDB, for example, transmission interface (E1 or T1), CRC-4, spare bits, synchronization source, receiver sensitivity, LBO, or STN Equipment. • Check that the transmission equipment at the other end is working correctly and all cables are connected correctly. • Check the transmission cable and replace it if necessary. • If the RBS is equipped with a DUG that has a GPS interface, then a GPS receiver can be installed and used as an alternative synchronization source. • Reset the DUG.

AO TF EC1:6.d: Multiple RBSs are configured as timing masters. Only one RBS is allowed to be a timing master in a TG cluster, that is, a set of RBSs connected to the same ESB. This fault is reported by the RBS that is unable to be a timing master and therefore disabled. This fault is probably caused by the following: • The BSC is unable to reconfigure an RBS as timing slave because of a link break. The RBS with a link break is reporting this fault. • Multiple logical TG clusters are defined for a single physical cluster connected to the same ESB. The RBSs that are not allowed to be timing master report this fault. • The RBS is unable to become a timing master because of an ESB cable fault.
AO TF EC1:6.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that the CF link between the BSC and RBS is established. If it is not established, then check the PCM line, transmission equipment, and so on. • Check the configuration of the TG cluster. Identity for the TGs with the BSC printout RXMOP. • Check the ESB cables.

AO TF EC1:7.d: The RBS is configured to be a timing slave with intracell holdover mode and the measurement of the ESB distribution delay between the timing master and this timing slave has failed. If the fault occurs while TF is trying to synchronize, the fault is reported after 5 minutes. If the fault occurs while TF is synchronized and measuring the ESB delay because of recalculation of the TF compensation value, TF goes into holdover mode. If the measurements do not succeed within the 2-minute holdover timeout period, the alarm is raised and TF is disabled. The likely causes are as follows: • The ESB cable is faulty or disconnected. • A terminator on the ESB is faulty or missing. Note: Only when TF mode is master or stand-alone.

AO TF EC2:0.d: There are several options: If TF mode is set to slave (TG parameter TFMODE = SA in the BSC) and ESB is used: • The External Synchronization Bus (ESB) reference, used as TG synchronization source, is unusable and TF is in holdover mode. If the ESB does not recover before holdover timeout, the class 1 fault AO TF EC1:0 is raised. If TF mode is set to slave (TG parameter TFMODE = SA in the BSC) and IDL2 is used: • The IDL2 reference, used as TG synchronization source, is unusable and TF is in holdover mode. If the IDL2 does not recover before holdover timeout, the class 1 fault AO TF EC1:0 is raised. • Note: The holdover period can be extended from 2 minutes to up to 24 hours if TF holdover mode is set to Intercell in the IDB. This requires that no TRXs in the RBS are included in a cell together with TRXs from a different RBS. If TF mode is set to standalone or master (TG parameter TFMODE = SA or MA in the BSC) and NGS is used: • The NGS reference, used as TG synchronization source is unusuable and TF is in holdover mode. If NGS does not recover before holdover timeout and no backup reference (GPS or PCM) is configured or available, the class 1 fault AO TF EC1:0 is raised. If TF mode is set to standalone or master (TG parameter TFMODE = SA or MA in the BSC) and GPS is used: • The GPS reference, used as synchronization source is unusuable and TF is in holdover mode. If GPS does not recover before holdover timeout and no backup reference (PCM) is configured or available, the class 1 fault AO TF EC1:0 is raised.
AO TF EC2:0.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. If ESB reference: • Check that synchronization of the master TG is without faults. • Check that the master TG has TF mode = master defined (TG parameter TFMODE = M in the BSC). • Check the hardware of the master TF source, (DXU if RBS 2000, DUG if RBS6000). • Check that the ESB cables between the master TG and slave TG are correctly connected and undamaged. If the cable is damaged, then replace it. • Check that termination plugs are mounted on all unconnected ESB connectors. If IDL2 reference: • If raised together with SO CF I2A:74/DU to DU Communication Lost • • See action for SO CF I2A:74 • Check that incoming synchronization of the SP (Synchronization Provider) is without faults. Check the DUW/DUL/DUS documentation for further analysis. • Check that the master TG has TF mode = master defined (TG parameter TFMODE = MA in the BSC). • Check the hardware of the master TF source, (DUG). • Check that the IDL2 cables between the master TG and slave TG are correctly connected and undamaged. If the cable is damaged, then replace it. If NGS reference: • If raised together with AO TF EC2:50/ Node Group Synch Source Lost • • See action for AO TF EC2:50. • If raised together with SO CF EC1:11 Node Group Synch Configuration Fault • • See action for SO CF EC1:11. • Check that incoming synchronization of the SP (Synchronization Provider) is without faults. Check the DUW/DUL/DUS documentation for further analysis. • Check that correct cabling is connecting defined RI ports for NGS according to IDB. Otherwise modify the IDB or reconnect cable according to the defined RI Ports. If GPS reference: • Check the GPS antenna. • Check the connection between the GPS receiver and the GPS antenna. • Check that the GPS antenna is placed so that it can receive signals from a sufficient number of satellites all the time. If it is not, then move the GPS antenna.

AO TF EC2:1.d: The synchronization reference from the PCM network is faulty (for example, too much jitter/wander) or missing. When a second PCM reference is not available, an AO TF EC1:1 class 1 alarm is raised if the PCM reference does not recover before the holdover period expires. The class 2 alarm is raised if the following applies: The variance of the TF estimated frequency exceeds a variance limit for a class 2 alarm. • Explanation:When the reference quality of the PCM is outside specification of G.823 and G.824, the BTS goes into holdover and the TF starts to estimate its own frequency quality. The trigger to go into holdover and start the estimation is when short-term wander on the PCM reference is more than 6 ppm for 25 seconds. The estimation process, using a Kalman filter, causes the variance of the estimated frequency to increase with time. • The alarm is raised after about 2 hours when temperature varies within +-10°C if the following conditions are fulfilled: • RBS with DUG or DXU excluding DXU-01, DXU-03, DXU-11 • More than 72 hours of operation locked to PCM, with temperature supervision. • PCM reference traceable to G.812 Type II/Stratum 2 • The alarm is raised after about 5 minutes if the above conditions are not fulfilled.
AO TF EC2:1.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • For RUG, follow the instructions in RBS 6000 DUG-RUG Troubleshooting Guidelines. • For RUS, follow the instructions in RBS 6000 DUG-RUS Troubleshooting Guidelines. • Check the PCM quality with the BSC printout command DTQUP: DIP. • Check that the transmission parameters are correctly set in the IDB, for example, transmission interface (E1 or T1), CRC-4, spare bits, synchronization source, receiver sensitivity, LBO, or STN Equipment. • Check that the transmission equipment in the other end is working correctly and all cables are connected correctly. • Check the transmission cable and replace it if necessary. • If the RBS is equipped with a DUG with a GPS interface, a GPS receiver can be installed as an alternative synchronization source. • Reset the DUG.

AO TF EC2:7.d: The RBS is configured to be a timing slave with intercell holdover mode and the measurement of the ESB distribution delay between the timing master and this timing slave has failed. If the fault occurs while TF is trying to synchronize, the fault is reported after 5 minutes. If the fault occurs while TF is synchronized and measuring the ESB delay caused by recalculation of the TF compensation value and the measurement does not succeed, the alarm is raised and TF is not disabled. No class 1 fault is reported when holdover mode is set to intercell. The likely causes are as follows: • The ESB cable is faulty or disconnected. • A terminator on the ESB is faulty or missing.

AO TF EC2:50.d: Master DUG acting as Synchronization Receiver in a Node Group cannot find any Node Group sync source and lost its communication to Synchronization Provider. This fault is likely raised when all CPRI links to Synchronization Provider are broken or the established CPRI links cannot select out any Node Group sync source.
AO TF EC2:50.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • If raised together with AO MCTR I1B:2/Lost Communication to Radio Unit • • See action for AO MCTR I1B:2. • Check that all DUs in the Node Group are powered-on. • Check the synchronization status and synchronization related alarms for all nodes in the Node Group that can act as synchronization provider. • Check that all the (R)RUSs in the Node Group are powered-on. • Check that correct cabling is connecting defined RI ports for the Node Group according to IDB. Otherwise modify the IDB or reconnect cable according to the defined RI Ports. • Check that all the DU to (R)RUS CPRI cables are correctly connected and in good condition. • Use the OMT function Check IDB to identify hardware/IDB inconsistence. • Reset the external DU that is not communicating correctly. • Reset the (R)RUS in the path that is not communicating correctly. • Reset the DUG. • Replace the DU to (R)RUS CPRI cables that are not communicating correctly. • Replace the SFP on the units that are not communicating correctly. • Replace the external DU that is not communicating correctly. • Replace the other DUG. • Replace the (R)RUS.

AO TF EC2:51.t: Node Group Sync External Communication Lost
AO TF EC2:51.d: The DUG in a Node Group has lost its NGS communication with RU over one or more ports configured as candidate RI port. The likely cause of this fault is that one or more CPRI links to RU are broken or the DUG have no NGS communication with RU over it.
AO TF EC2:51.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • If raised together with AO MCTR I1B:2/Lost Communication to Radio Unit • • See action for AO MCTR I1B:2. • Check that all DUs in the Node Group are powered-on. • Check that all the (R)RUSs in the Node Group are powered-on. • Check that correct cabling is connecting defined RI ports for the Node Group according to IDB. Otherwise modify the IDB or reconnect cable according to the defined RI Ports. • Check that all the DU to (R)RUS CPRI cables are correctly connected and in good condition. • Use the OMT function Check IDB to identify hardware/IDB inconsistence. • Reset the external DU that is not communicating correctly. • Reset the (R)RUS in the path that is not communicating correctly. • Reset the DUG. • Replace the DU to (R)RUS CPRI cables that are not communicating correctly. • Replace the SFP on the units that are not communicating correctly. • Replace the external DU that is not communicating correctly. • Replace the other DUG. • Replace the (R)RUS.

AO TF EC2:52.t: Node Group Sync Disqualified Passive PCM Ref
AO TF EC2:52.d: This fault will be raised when the GSM node is in the node group and detected a disqualified passive PCM reference.
AO TF EC2:52.a: To resolve the alarm, do the following: • Check PCM connection is in good condition. If the alarm remains, do the following: • Check Node Group Reference is in good condition. • This alarm doesn’t impact traffic and node work normally, because the passive PCM reference is not the current using reference.

AO TF EC2:54.d: DUG in a Node Group cannot find any Node Group sync source or can not distribute the NGS synchronization to the rest of the node group. This fault is likely raised when all CPRI communication links dedicated for NGS on the DUG are lost.
AO TF EC2:54.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • If raised together with AO MCTR I1B:2/Lost Communication to Radio Unit • • See action for AO MCTR I1B:2. • Check that all DUs in the Node Group are powered-on. • Check the DUG and synchronization signal is correctly connected and in good condition. • Check that all the (R)RUSs in the Node Group are powered-on. • Check that correct cabling is connecting defined RI ports for the Node Group according to IDB. Otherwise modify the IDB or reconnect cable according to the defined RI Ports. • Check that all the DU to (R)RUS CPRI cables are correctly connected and in good condition. • Use the OMT function Check IDB to identify hardware/IDB inconsistence. • Reset the external DU that is not communicating correctly. • Reset the (R)RUS in the path that is not communicating correctly. • Reset the DUG. • Replace the DU to (R)RUS CPRI cables that are not communicating correctly. • Replace the SFP on the units that are not communicating correctly. • Replace the external DU that is not communicating correctly. • Replace the other DU. • Replace the (R)RUS.

AO TF EC2:56.t: Node Group Sync Disqualified Active PCM Ref
AO TF EC2:56.d: This fault will be raised when the GSM act as SP in the Node Group and detected a disqualified active PCM reference.
AO TF EC2:56.a: To resolve the alarm, do the following: • Check PCM connection is in good condition. • Check Node Group Reference is in good condition. If the alarm remains, do the following: • Configure DUG’s Node Priority as Node Group Synchronization Receiver Node, set a low priority in IDB of DUG. • Reset the DUG. • Check the DUG and synchronization signal is correctly connected and in good condition as Node Group Synchronization Receiver. OR • Plug-in a real GPS for GSM DUG20, so GPS can be the Sync Reference when GSM is acting as Node Group Sync Provider, configure also in IDB for GPS. • Reset the DUG. • Check the DUG and synchronization signal is correctly connected and in good condition. If the alarm remains, consult next level of maintenance support.

AO TS EC1:3.d: The speech/data frames coming from the BSC to the TS are missing or corrupted. This is most likely a fault in the BSC (for example, no TRA allocated, no connection in Group-Switch, and so on) or in the Abis transmission path.

AO MCTR I1B:1.d: The temperature of the RUS/RRUS/Radio is below or above normal conditional range. The fault ceases when the temperature is back within the normal conditional range. In the non-destruction range the RUS/RRUS/Radio takes autonomous actions to protect itself from being damaged. No function is guaranteed. When the fault ceases the system restarts the RUS to ensure functionality. In the exceptional operation range the RUS/RRUS/Radio has full functionality and degraded performance. The likely causes of this fault are as follows: • If the fault is issued together with a fan fault, then the most likely cause of the fault is a faulty fan unit. • If the alarm is raised on only one RUS/RRUS/Radio, then it is likely that the unit has developed a fault, in which case it is likely that another fault also has been issued for that unit. • If several RUSs/RRUSs/Radios from different subracks have issued the fault, then the most likely cause is a fault at the site, in the RBS air-conditioning or in the cooling system. • A mismatch in the antenna system can cause this fault to be set on high levels of reflected power.
AO MCTR I1B:1.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • For RUS, follow the instructions in RBS 6000 DUG-RUS Troubleshooting Guidelines. • If applicable, make sure dummy plates and air guides are correctly installed in the RBS. • If applicable, check the filters and the climate unit. • Inspect the RBS to ensure that there are no leaks and that nothing is obstructing the airflow in and around the unit issuing the alarm. Before inspecting an RRUS, remove the front cover. • If applicable, inspect the site cooling and heating systems to ensure that they are functioning correctly. • Test the climate system. • Check the TX cables/feeders, cable connections inside and outside the cabinet and antennas, for example, with Antenna System SWR tests. For information about how to perform an SWR test, see document Verifying System Antennas or document Antenna System Tests for the relevant RBS. • Reset the RUS/RRUS/Radio. • Replace the RUS/RRUS/Radio. ru: SO CF RU:40 - Antenna
SO CF I2A:33.d: There is an imbalance in signal strength between the receiver paths for one or more TRXs. Depending on which RX path has the lowest signal strength, one or more of the related faults are also raised. To avoid false alarms, the fault has a long filter time that depends on the traffic load. Therefore, the fault can occur several days after installation. Despite the long filter time, a single mobile might cause an alarm if the call is made when the traffic is low and the call continues for a long time in an area with poor coverage, for example, during nights and behind the antenna. When traffic increases, the alarm normally ceases. To correct this kind of alarm, the radio cell planning must be revised.
SO CF I2A:33.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. Note: Long filter time – do not use reset until all actions have been performed. If other alarms are raised on the same RX path, this might also be the cause of the RX diversity alarm. If present, then correct such alarms first. • For RBS2x06, follow the instructions in RBS 2x06 Troubleshooting Guidelines. • For RBS2x16, follow the instructions in RBS 2x16 Troubleshooting Guidelines. • Use the raised RX I2A faults to identify which RXs, and thereby which RX path, are faulty. The RX path identifies the connection to investigate. • Check that cables are connected to the correct CDUs and antennas. The OMT Radio view shows how the IDB is defined regarding the connections. • Check that the correct RX Diversity mode is defined in the BSC (RX parameter RXD with possible values A, B, AB, and ABCD). SO CF I2A:41.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that all TRU circuit breakers on the IDM are switched on, and any fuses on the TDM are intact. • Check that the defined TRUs/DRUs in the IDB correspond to the TRUs/DRUs in the RBS. If the cable is damaged, then replace it. • Check that termination plugs are mounted on all unconnected bus connectors. • For RBSs 2101, 2102, 2103, or 2202: Check that the setting of the TRU backplane switches is correct in both the master cabinet and the extension cabinet (if present). • Reset the TRU/DRU not communicating correctly with the DXU. • Reset the DXU. • Replace the TRU/DRU not communicating correctly with the DXU. • Replace the DXU. • Replace the local bus cable between the DXU/ECU backplane and TRU backplane. • Replace the TRU backplane. • Replace the DXU/ECU backplane.

SO CF I2A:42.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check that all ECU circuit breakers or fuses on the IDM are on or intact. • If applicable, check that the external bus between the cabinets is correctly connected and undamaged. If the cable is damaged, then replace it. • Check that termination plugs are mounted on all unconnected bus connectors. • If applicable, check that the DXU/ECU backplane switches are set correctly in both the master cabinet and the extension cabinet. • Reset the ECU not communicating with the DXU. • Reset the DXU. • For RBS 2101: Switch off and pull out the TRUs temporarily. Reset the ECU. • Replace the ECU not communicating with the DXU. • Replace the DXU/ECU backplane.

SO CF I2A:47.d: Antenna hopping is not possible, either because of the configuration received from the BSC or site constraints. The BSS feature BTS Power Saving might raise this alarm when the traffic load is continuously low. The alarm has a filtering time of one week before the alarm is raised. Only configurations with CDU-G, CDU-K, CDU-J, CDU-L, or DRU support antenna hopping. To enable antenna hopping, at least one antenna system must include two enabled TXs, connected to separate antennas.
SO CF I2A:47.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check the BSC configuration of Antenna Hopping. • Read the IDB and use the Radio view in the OMT to check how the IDB is defined regarding the connections. • Undefine Antenna Hopping with the BSC if not feasible. Note: Manual definition of Antenna Hopping = On/Off in the IDB is overruled/redefined by the BSC configuration.

ru: SO CF RU:48 - GPS Receiver
SO CF RU:49 - GPS Receiver DXU Cable
SO CF I2A:48.d: For GPS receiver: • The defined GPS receiver has a hardware fault. If no backup synchronization source (PCM) is available, fault AO TF I1B:2 is raised. For GPS receiver DXU cable: • There is no communication between the DXU and the defined GPS receiver. If no backup synchronization source (PCM) is available, fault AO TF I1B:2 is raised.
SO CF I2A:48.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. For GPS receiver: • Remove the class 1 alarm, if present, by using PCM as backup synchronization source. This is done by defining the TF parameter SYNCSRC = DEFAULT in the BSC. • Check the GPS receiver and its receiver chain, that is, the antenna and cables. • Disconnect the power to the GPS receiver, for example, by disconnecting the connector in the OVP module. Wait a few minutes, then reconnect the power. For GPS receiver DXU cable: • Remove the class 1 alarm, if present, by using PCM as backup synchronization source. This is done by defining the TF parameter SYNCSRC = DEFAULT in the BSC. • Check the connection between the DXU and the GPS receiver. • Disconnect the power to the GPS receiver, for example, by disconnecting the connector in the OVP module. Wait a few minutes, then reconnect the power. • Check the power supply to the GPS receiver by checking the DC indicator in the OVP module. • Check the GPS receiver and its receiver chain, that is, the antenna and cables. • If no GPS receiver is required, then use Define GPS Parameters in the OMT to set GPS present = No in the IDB.

SO CF I2A:49.t: Battery Backup Time Shorter Than Expected
SO CF I2A:49.d: The battery backup time is shorter than the expected battery backup time, as defined in the IDB. Cease criteria are either: • Next test measures a backup time longer than expected. • The test is disabled. • The start date of the test is changed to a future date. • The expected time is changed.
SO CF I2A:49.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check in the IDB that the defined Battery Backup Time Test Parameters are correct. • Test the battery according to the supplier specifications. • Replace the batteries.

SO CF I2A:50.d: The RBS is running on batteries. Unless external power is restored the RBS eventually turns itself off.
SO CF I2A:50.a: Follow the instructions below until the fault is resolved. • Check the external power supply. • Check the ACCU. • Check the PSUs. • Check the defined Power System for each cabinet in the IDB.

ru: SO CF RU:40 - Antenna
SO CF I2A:57.d: This fault is raised if the difference in signal strength between two antennas in the same antenna system exceeds the limits defined by the Define RX Path Imbalance Parameters in the OMT. If the class 1 limit is exceeded, related fault AO TX I1B:35 is also raised and the TX disabled. The supervision of this fault is based on measurements over a long period; hence the fault does not cease as soon as the fault is corrected. The RX imbalance monitor must therefore be used to verify the correction of the fault.
SO CF I2A:57.a: Follow the instructions below: • Check the defined RX path invariance limits using the Define RX Path Imbalance Parameters function in the OMT for the faulty antenna system. • Check the TX cables/feeders, cable connections inside and outside the cabinet and antennas, for example, with Antenna System SWR tests. For information about how to perform an SWR test, see document Verifying System Antennas or document Antenna System Tests for the relevant RBS. • When the fault is corrected, reset the TRU to cease the fault immediately. Note: If the fault is not resolved, it is reported again as soon as the minimum number of samples is collected.

SO CF EC2:10.d: There is a failure in the AC mains or DC supply, or an AC input cable to a PSU or the climate unit is disconnected. The ACCU might also be faulty or wrongly strapped.

Danger! Electric shock risk. Avoid both direct and indirect contact with parts connected to mains power as this is likely to be fatal. Switch off the mains power before starting work. Document RBS Installation Instructions must be read before starting the procedure. • If applicable, check that the AC mains connections and straps in the ACCU/AC mains connection box are in accordance with the AC voltage. • Replace the PSU. Note: If this fault and faults SO CF I2A:23, 29, and 37 are raised at the same time, then contact Ericsson for special trouble shooting guidelines.

If all ALNAs/TMAs to an RX are faulty, fault AO RX I1B:1 is raised and the RX disabled (AO RX I2A RX Path Lost on Receiver Side faults are ceased), unless TMA Type = GSM/TDMA bypass is defined. TMA bypass configurations require that the installed ALNAs/TMAs support the by-pass function.
